name: Kingbright L-7113ID 5 mm red LED
//: True of Kingbright L-7113ID only: T-1 3/4 (5 mm) through-hole lamp, High Efficiency Red GaAsP/GaP chip, red diffused lens, datasheet Spec No DSAA6645, Rev V.29A (09/04/2020). Other '5 mm red LEDs', and other Kingbright suffixes (L-7113SRD, L-7113HD, L-7113GD...), have different chips, forward voltages and viewing angles. Status indicator on a breadboard build, so through-hole on purpose.

needs.note: A GPIO drives the anode HIGH through the series resistor in host_parts; the cathode goes to ground, so the LED is lit when the pin is 1. Never connect the anode straight to the pin: with no resistor the only limit is the GPIO's own drive, far past this part's 30 mA DC maximum.

power.note: Cathode to the board's ground. The current through it is the series resistor's, at most a few mA here; this pin is the return, not a supply input.

pin_order_proof.source: Pad 1 = anode, pad 2 = cathode. Datasheet page 1, Package Dimensions: the lead labelled 'Cathode' is drawn 1.5 (+/-1) mm SHORTER than the other, so the LONGER lead is the anode; the end view draws a flat on the flange rim (diameter 5.9 mm) on the cathode lead's side. The drawing labels the cathode lead and draws the flat but does not label the flat in words.

//footprint: A stand-in for the two leads, not the LED's outline: pinrow2 is two through-holes at 2.54 mm, which is the drawing's lead spacing (2.54 (0.1) mm, measured where the leads leave the package, page 1). The silkscreen is a pin header's, not the 5.9 mm round flange with its cathode flat, so placement must use body_mm, not the footprint, to keep clear of neighbours. Kingbright's recommended PCB layout (page 1) is two holes of 0.9 mm diameter at 2.54 mm; check pinrow2's drill against it before a PCB is ordered. The leads are 0.5 mm square (+0.25/-0.1).

body_mm.note: Plan view of the LED standing upright: the flange rim is diameter 5.9 (0.232) mm, which is the widest part and so the one an overlap check needs. The lens is diameter 5.0 (0.197) mm; lens plus flange stand 8.6 (0.339) mm above the lead exit, flange 1.0 mm max thick; leads 27 mm min. Tolerance +/-0.25 mm unless noted.

forward_voltage_v.note: TYPICAL, at IF = 10 mA, TA = 25 C ('Forward Voltage IF = 10mA ... Typ. 1.9'); tolerance +/-0.1 V (note 2); TC of VF -1.9 mV/C. The datasheet prints no VF at 5 mA; it is somewhat lower there (a diode's VF falls with current; the page-3 curve was not read numerically), so a resistor computed from 1.9 V passes a little more than asked.

forward_voltage_max_v.note: Maximum at IF = 10 mA, TA = 25 C.

max_continuous_current_ma.note: 'DC Forward Current IF 30 mA' at TA = 25 C. Peak 160 mA at 1/10 duty, 0.1 ms pulse; power dissipation 75 mW; reverse voltage 5 V. The page-3 derating curve lowers the permissible current at high ambient; its exact knee is a curve, not a printed number.

peak_wavelength_nm.note: Typical, IF = 10 mA. Dominant wavelength 617 nm; spectral bandwidth 45 nm.

viewing_angle_deg.note: 2 theta 1/2 = 30 degrees (full angle to half intensity). Narrow for a diffused lamp: the indicator is bright on-axis and dim from the side, so aim it where it will be looked at. Luminous intensity 50 mcd typ (25 min) at 10 mA.

host_parts.why: limits the LED's current from a 3.3 V GPIO; 5 mA is bright enough for an indicator, well under the DC maximum

host_requirements: A series resistor between the GPIO and the anode, always: without it the LED's current is set only by the pin's drive strength, and it either runs far past 30 mA or droops the pin's level.

Keep it off the chip's strapping pins: an LED and resistor to ground load the pin while the chip samples its straps at reset, and can change how it boots. (Reasoned from the circuit, not from this datasheet.)
On a breadboard: the LONG lead (anode) goes to the resistor; the short lead, on the side of the flat in the rim, goes to ground. Once the leads are trimmed equal, the flat is the mark that survives.

wokwi.stand_in: Wokwi's LED: lights on current; its forward voltage and brightness are not this part's
